// This file simulates WebSocket behavior for local development
class MockWebSocket {
  private listeners: Record<string, ((data: any) => void)[]> = {};
  private teamId: string | null = null;
  private connected: boolean = false;
  private mockMessages = [
    {
      id: "auto-msg-1",
      agent: "Manager",
      content: "I'm analyzing the current task...",
      timestamp: "",
      type: "text"
    },
    {
      id: "auto-msg-2",
      agent: "Planner",
      content: "Based on our current progress, I recommend we focus on implementing the shopping cart functionality next.",
      timestamp: "",
      type: "text"
    },
    {
      id: "auto-msg-3",
      agent: "Coder",
      content: "I'll start working on the ShoppingCart component. It will need to handle adding/removing items and updating quantities.",
      timestamp: "",
      type: "text"
    },
    {
      id: "auto-msg-4",
      agent: "Tester",
      content: "I'll prepare test cases for the shopping cart, focusing on edge cases like empty cart, item quantity limits, and price calculations.",
      timestamp: "",
      type: "text"
    }
  ];
  private messageInterval: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
  
  constructor() {
    console.log("Mock WebSocket initialized");
  }
  
  public connect(url: string): void {
    setTimeout(() => {
      this.connected = true;
      this.emit('connect', {});
      console.log("Mock WebSocket connected");
    }, 500);
  }
  
  public on(event: string, callback: (data: any) => void): void {
    if (!this.listeners[event]) {
      this.listeners[event] = [];
    }
    this.listeners[event].push(callback);
  }
  
  public emit(event: string, data: any): void {
    if (this.listeners[event]) {
      this.listeners[event].forEach(callback => callback(data));
    }
  }
  
  public joinTeam(teamId: string): void {
    this.teamId = teamId;
    console.log(`Joined team: ${teamId}`);
    this.startMockMessageStream();
  }
  
  private startMockMessageStream(): void {
    if (this.messageInterval) {
      clearInterval(this.messageInterval);
    }
    
    let messageIndex = 0;
    
    // Send a message every 10-20 seconds
    this.messageInterval = setInterval(() => {
      if (!this.connected || !this.teamId) return;
      
      const message = {...this.mockMessages[messageIndex]};
      message.timestamp = new Date().toISOString();
      message.id = `auto-msg-${Date.now()}`;
      
      this.emit('message', message);
      
      messageIndex = (messageIndex + 1) % this.mockMessages.length;
    }, Math.random() * 10000 + 10000); // Between 10 and 20 seconds
  }
  
  public disconnect(): void {
    this.connected = false;
    if (this.messageInterval) {
      clearInterval(this.messageInterval);
      this.messageInterval = null;
    }
    console.log("Mock WebSocket disconnected");
  }
  
  public isConnected(): boolean {
    return this.connected;
  }
}

export default MockWebSocket; 


--- FILE: C:\Users\urib9\projects\Hive mind\archive\old-ui\services\screenshot.ts ---
import { invoke } from '@tauri-apps/api/tauri';
import { appWindow } from '@tauri-apps/api/window';
import { save } from '@tauri-apps/api/dialog';
import { writeTextFile, createDir, exists, readDir } from '@tauri-apps/api/fs';
import { desktopDir, join } from '@tauri-apps/api/path';
import html2canvas from 'html2canvas';

interface ScreenshotOptions {
  captureActiveElement?: boolean;
  includeMetadata?: boolean;
  quality?: number;
}

interface ScreenshotMetadata {
  timestamp: string;
  url: string;
  viewport: {
    width: number;
    height: number;
  };
  elementSelector?: string;
}

/**
 * Service for capturing screenshots of the UI for agent awareness
 */
export class ScreenshotService {
  private readonly screenshotsFolder = 'hive-mind-screenshots';
  private initialized = false;
  
  constructor() {
    this.init();
  }
  
  private async init() {
    try {
      // Create screenshots directory if it doesn't exist
      const desktopPath = await desktopDir();
      const screenshotsPath = await join(desktopPath, this.screenshotsFolder);
      
      if (!(await exists(screenshotsPath))) {
        await createDir(screenshotsPath, { recursive: true });
      }
      
      this.initialized = true;
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Failed to initialize screenshot service:', error);
    }
  }
  
  /**
   * Captures a screenshot of the current UI
   */
  async captureFullScreen(options: ScreenshotOptions = {}): Promise<string | null> {
    if (!this.initialized) await this.init();
    
    try {
      // Use html2canvas to capture the full page
      const canvas = await html2canvas(document.body, {
        scale: 1,
        useCORS: true,
        logging: false,
        allowTaint: true,
        ...options
      });
      
      const screenshotData = canvas.toDataURL('image/png');
      const filePath = await this.saveScreenshot(screenshotData, options);
      return filePath;
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Failed to capture screenshot:', error);
      return null;
    }
  }
  
  /**
   * Captures a specific element in the UI
   */
  async captureElement(selector: string, options: ScreenshotOptions = {}): Promise<string | null> {
    if (!this.initialized) await this.init();
    
    try {
      const element = document.querySelector(selector);
      if (!element) {
        console.error(`Element with selector ${selector} not found`);
        return null;
      }
      
      // Use html2canvas to capture the element
      const screenshotData = await this.captureElementToDataUrl(element as HTMLElement);
      
      const filePath = await this.saveScreenshot(
        screenshotData, 
        { ...options, captureActiveElement: true }
      );
      return filePath;
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Failed to capture element screenshot:', error);
      return null;
    }
  }
  
  private async captureElementToDataUrl(element: HTMLElement): Promise<string> {
    const canvas = await html2canvas(element, {
      scale: 1,
      useCORS: true,
      logging: false,
      allowTaint: true
    });
    
    return canvas.toDataURL('image/png');
  }
  
  private async saveScreenshot(
    dataUrl: string, 
    options: ScreenshotOptions
  ): Promise<string> {
    const desktopPath = await desktopDir();
    const screenshotsPath = await join(desktopPath, this.screenshotsFolder);
    
    const timestamp = new Date().toISOString().replace(/:/g, '-');
    const filename = `screenshot-${timestamp}.png`;
    const filePath = await join(screenshotsPath, filename);
    
    // Convert data URL to blob data
    const base64Data = dataUrl.replace(/^data:image\/\w+;base64,/, '');
    
    // Save metadata if requested
    if (options.includeMetadata) {
      const metadata: ScreenshotMetadata = {
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        url: window.location.href,
        viewport: {
          width: window.innerWidth,
          height: window.innerHeight
        },
        elementSelector: options.captureActiveElement ? document.activeElement?.tagName : undefined
      };
      
      const metadataFilePath = await join(screenshotsPath, `screenshot-${timestamp}.json`);
      await writeTextFile(metadataFilePath, JSON.stringify(metadata, null, 2));
    }
    
    // Save the screenshot
    await writeTextFile(filePath, base64Data, { append: false });
    
    console.log(`Screenshot saved to ${filePath}`);
    return filePath;
  }
  
  /**
   * Provides the latest screenshot to agents
   */
  async getLatestScreenshotForAgent(): Promise<{ path: string; base64Data?: string } | null> {
    if (!this.initialized) await this.init();
    
    try {
      const desktopPath = await desktopDir();
      const screenshotsPath = await join(desktopPath, this.screenshotsFolder);
      
      // Read the directory to find all screenshots
      const entries = await readDir(screenshotsPath);
      
      // Filter for PNG files and sort by creation time (filename contains timestamp)
      const pngFiles = entries
        .filter(entry => entry.name && entry.name.endsWith('.png'))
        .sort((a, b) => {
          // Sort in descending order (newest first)
          return (b.name || '').localeCompare(a.name || '');
        });
      
      if (pngFiles.length === 0) {
        return null;
      }
      
      // Return the most recent screenshot
      const latestScreenshot = pngFiles[0];
      return { 
        path: latestScreenshot.path
      };
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Failed to get latest screenshot:', error);
      return null;
    }
  }
}

export const screenshotService = new ScreenshotService(); 


--- FILE: C:\Users\urib9\projects\Hive mind\archive\old-ui\services\websocket.ts ---
import { WS_URL, AUTH_TOKEN_KEY } from '../config';
import MockWebSocket from './mockWebSocket';

type MessageHandler = (data: any) => void;
type ConnectionHandler = () => void;

class WebSocketService {
  private socket: WebSocket | null = null;
  private mockSocket: MockWebSocket | null = null;
  private messageHandlers: Map<string, MessageHandler[]> = new Map();
  private onConnectHandlers: ConnectionHandler[] = [];
  private onDisconnectHandlers: ConnectionHandler[] = [];
  private reconnectTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  private isConnecting = false;
  private useMockSocket = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' || window.location.search.includes('mock=true');

  constructor() {
    this.connect = this.connect.bind(this);
    this.disconnect = this.disconnect.bind(this);
    this.send = this.send.bind(this);
    this.onMessage = this.onMessage.bind(this);
    this.onConnect = this.onConnect.bind(this);
    this.onDisconnect = this.onDisconnect.bind(this);
    this.handleMessage = this.handleMessage.bind(this);
    this.joinTeam = this.joinTeam.bind(this);
  }

  connect(): void {
    if (this.useMockSocket) {
      console.log('Using mock WebSocket');
      this.connectMock();
      return;
    }

    if (this.socket && (this.socket.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN || this.socket.readyState === WebSocket.CONNECTING)) {
      return;
    }

    if (this.isConnecting) {
      return;
    }

    this.isConnecting = true;

    const token = localStorage.getItem(AUTH_TOKEN_KEY);
    const url = token ? `${WS_URL}?token=${token}` : WS_URL;
    
    this.socket = new WebSocket(url);
    
    this.socket.onopen = () => {
      this.isConnecting = false;
      this.onConnectHandlers.forEach(handler => handler());
      
      if (this.reconnectTimer) {
        clearTimeout(this.reconnectTimer);
        this.reconnectTimer = null;
      }
    };
    
    this.socket.onclose = () => {
      this.isConnecting = false;
      this.onDisconnectHandlers.forEach(handler => handler());
      
      if (!this.reconnectTimer) {
        this.reconnectTimer = setTimeout(() => {
          this.connect();
        }, 3000);
      }
    };
    
    this.socket.onmessage = (event) => {
      try {
        const data = JSON.parse(event.data);
        this.handleMessage(data);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Error parsing WebSocket message:', error);
      }
    };
    
    this.socket.onerror = (error) => {
      console.error('WebSocket error:', error);
      this.isConnecting = false;
    };
  }
  
  private connectMock(): void {
    if (this.mockSocket) {
      return;
    }
    
    this.mockSocket = new MockWebSocket();
    
    this.mockSocket.on('connect', () => {
      this.onConnectHandlers.forEach(handler => handler());
    });
    
    this.mockSocket.on('message', (message) => {
      this.handleMessage({ type: 'message', payload: message });
    });
    
    this.mockSocket.connect(WS_URL);
  }
  
  joinTeam(teamId: string): void {
    if (this.useMockSocket && this.mockSocket) {
      this.mockSocket.joinTeam(teamId);
      return;
    }
    
    this.send('join_team', { team_id: teamId });
  }
  
  disconnect(): void {
    if (this.useMockSocket && this.mockSocket) {
      this.mockSocket.disconnect();
      this.mockSocket = null;
      return;
    }
    
    if (this.socket) {
      this.socket.close();
      this.socket = null;
    }
    
    if (this.reconnectTimer) {
      clearTimeout(this.reconnectTimer);
      this.reconnectTimer = null;
    }
  }
  
  send(type: string, payload: any): boolean {
    if (this.useMockSocket && this.mockSocket) {
      this.mockSocket.emit(type, payload);
      return true;
    }
    
    if (!this.socket || this.socket.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) {
      return false;
    }
    
    this.socket.send(JSON.stringify({ type, payload }));
    return true;
  }
  
  onMessage(type: string, handler: MessageHandler): () => void {
    if (!this.messageHandlers.has(type)) {
      this.messageHandlers.set(type, []);
    }
    
    const handlers = this.messageHandlers.get(type)!;
    handlers.push(handler);
    
    return () => {
      const index = handlers.indexOf(handler);
      if (index !== -1) {
        handlers.splice(index, 1);
      }
    };
  }
  
  onConnect(handler: ConnectionHandler): () => void {
    this.onConnectHandlers.push(handler);
    
    return () => {
      const index = this.onConnectHandlers.indexOf(handler);
      if (index !== -1) {
        this.onConnectHandlers.splice(index, 1);
      }
    };
  }
  
  onDisconnect(handler: ConnectionHandler): () => void {
    this.onDisconnectHandlers.push(handler);
    
    return () => {
      const index = this.onDisconnectHandlers.indexOf(handler);
      if (index !== -1) {
        this.onDisconnectHandlers.splice(index, 1);
      }
    };
  }
  
  private handleMessage(data: { type: string; payload: any }): void {
    if (!data || !data.type) {
      return;
    }
    
    const handlers = this.messageHandlers.get(data.type);
    if (handlers) {
      handlers.forEach(handler => handler(data.payload));
    }
  }
}

// Create singleton instance
const websocketService = new WebSocketService();

export default websocketService;

import { API_BASE_URL } from '../config';

/**
 * Checks if the API is accessible
 * @returns Promise that resolves to true if accessible, false otherwise
 */
export const checkApiConnection = async (): Promise<boolean> => {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${API_BASE_URL}/health`, {
      method: 'GET',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      },
      // Timeout after 3 seconds
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000),
    });
    
    return response.ok;
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn('API connection check failed:', error);
    return false;
  }
};

/**
 * Displays a warning banner if the API is not accessible
 */
export const showApiWarningIfNeeded = async () => {
  try {
    const isConnected = await checkApiConnection();
    
    if (!isConnected) {
      const warningDiv = document.createElement('div');
      warningDiv.style.position = 'fixed';
      warningDiv.style.top = '0';
      warningDiv.style.left = '0';
      warningDiv.style.right = '0';
      warningDiv.style.backgroundColor = '#FFA500';
      warningDiv.style.color = '#000';
      warningDiv.style.padding = '10px';
      warningDiv.style.textAlign = 'center';
      warningDiv.style.zIndex = '9999';
      warningDiv.innerHTML = `
        <strong>Warning:</strong> Unable to connect to the backend API at <code>${API_BASE_URL}</code>. 
        The UI will use mock data for demonstration purposes. Some features may not work properly.
      `;
      
      document.body.appendChild(warningDiv);
      
      // Enable mock API data automatically
      window.localStorage.setItem('USE_MOCK_API', 'true');
      (window as any).USE_MOCK_API = true;
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error in API warning check:', error);
    // Ensure UI doesn't block even if this check fails
    window.localStorage.setItem('USE_MOCK_API', 'true');
    (window as any).USE_MOCK_API = true;
  }
};

/**
 * Use this function to get either mock data or real data
 * based on API availability
 * @param mockData Mock data to return if API is not available
 * @param apiFn Function to call to get real data
 */
export const getDataWithFallback = async <T>(mockData: T, apiFn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> => {
  if ((window as any).USE_MOCK_API || window.localStorage.getItem('USE_MOCK_API') === 'true') {
    return Promise.resolve(mockData);
  }
  
  try {
    return await apiFn();
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn('API call failed, using mock data:', error);
    window.localStorage.setItem('USE_MOCK_API', 'true');
    (window as any).USE_MOCK_API = true;
    return mockData;
  }
};

--- FILE: C:\Users\urib9\projects\Hive mind\docs\screenshot-mechanism.md ---
# UI Screenshot Mechanism for LLM Agent Awareness

## Overview

This feature allows LLM agents to "see" the UI they've created through screenshot capture capabilities. It enables agents to capture the current state of the user interface and share it with other agents, promoting a more comprehensive understanding of the UI's visual representation.

## Implementation Details

The screenshot mechanism consists of the following components:

### 1. Screenshot Service (`src/services/screenshot.ts`)

A service that handles the core screenshot functionality:
- Captures full-screen screenshots of the current UI
- Captures specific DOM elements using selectors
- Manages screenshot storage and metadata
- Provides access to the latest screenshots for agents

### 2. React Hook (`src/hooks/useScreenshot.ts`)

A custom React hook that wraps the screenshot service functionality:
- Manages state related to capturing screenshots
- Handles capturing, errors, and loading states
- Provides a clean interface for React components

### 3. UI Component (`src/components/ScreenshotTool.tsx`)

A reusable React component that provides UI controls for:
- Capturing full-screen screenshots
- Capturing specific elements using CSS selectors
- Displaying the latest screenshot path

### 4. Integration with Agent Communication

- Screenshots are shared through the WebSocket communication system
- System messages inform users when screenshots are captured
- A dedicated API endpoint for recording and retrieving screenshots

## How It Works

1. **Capture**: When a user triggers a screenshot through the UI, the `html2canvas` library captures the current UI state.
2. **Storage**: The screenshot is saved to the filesystem with metadata about when and where it was captured.
3. **Sharing**: The screenshot path is shared with agents, notifying them that a new visual representation is available.
4. **Access**: Agents can access the screenshot to gain visual understanding of the UI state.

## Usage for Agents

Agents can use the screenshot mechanism to:
- Verify that UI changes have been applied correctly
- Understand the current visual layout of components
- Identify potential UI issues or improvements
- Reference specific UI elements in their communications

## Technical Requirements

- **Client-side**: 
  - html2canvas library for DOM capturing
  - React for UI components
  - Tauri's filesystem API for storage

- **Server-side**:
  - API endpoints for screenshot metadata
  - WebSocket for real-time notifications

## Future Improvements

- Add automated screenshot capture on significant UI changes
- Implement visual diffing to highlight UI changes between screenshots
- Create AI-specific image analysis to enhance agent understanding of UI elements
- Add annotation capabilities for agents to highlight specific elements

# PowerShell script to change VS Code branch

param (
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [switch]$List,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [string]$Client,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [string]$Branch,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [string]$Commit,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [string]$Url = "http://localhost:5000",

    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [switch]$CreateMock,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [switch]$GrantPermission,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [switch]$DenyPermission
)

Write-Host "DEBUG: PowerShell script raw parameters received:" -ForegroundColor Magenta
Write-Host "  List: $List" -ForegroundColor Magenta
Write-Host "  Client: '$($Client)'" -ForegroundColor Magenta # Enclose in quotes to see if it's empty or has spaces
Write-Host "  Branch: '$($Branch)'" -ForegroundColor Magenta
Write-Host "  Commit: '$($Commit)'" -ForegroundColor Magenta
Write-Host "  Url: '$($Url)'" -ForegroundColor Magenta
Write-Host "  CreateMock: '$($CreateMock)'" -ForegroundColor Magenta
Write-Host "  GrantPermission: '$($GrantPermission)'" -ForegroundColor Magenta
Write-Host "  DenyPermission: '$($DenyPermission)'" -ForegroundColor Magenta
Write-Host "--- End DEBUG ---" -ForegroundColor Magenta

# Trim leading/trailing backslashes from string parameters if they exist
if ($Client -is [string]) { $Client = $Client.Trim('\') }
if ($Branch -is [string]) { $Branch = $Branch.Trim('\') }
if ($Commit -is [string]) { $Commit = $Commit.Trim('\') }

Write-Host "DEBUG: PowerShell script parameters after trimming:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "  Client: '$($Client)'" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "  Branch: '$($Branch)'" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "  Commit: '$($Commit)'" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "--- End DEBUG ---" -ForegroundColor Cyan

# Check if backend is running
try {
    $null = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $Url -Method Get -ErrorAction Stop
    Write-Host "Backend is running at $Url" -ForegroundColor Green
} catch {
    Write-Host "Backend is not running. Starting the backend..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    
    # Try to start the backend
    Start-Process -FilePath "docker-compose" -ArgumentList "up -d hive-mind-backend" -NoNewWindow -Wait
    
    # Wait for backend to start
    Write-Host "Waiting for backend to start..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
}

# Build arguments for the Python script
$pythonArgs = @("change-vscode-branch.py") # Initialize with script name only

$pythonArgs += "--url", $Url # Add URL and its value

if ($List) {
    $pythonArgs += "--list"
}

if ($Client) {
    $pythonArgs += "--client", $Client # Add client flag and its value
}

if ($Branch) {
    $pythonArgs += "--branch", $Branch # Add branch flag and its value
}

if ($Commit) {
    $pythonArgs += "--commit", $Commit # Add commit flag and its value
}

# Create a mock client if requested (will use the new direct API)
if ($CreateMock) {
    Write-Host "Creating a mock VS Code client..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    try {
        $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Method POST -Uri "$Url/api/vscode/mock" -ContentType "application/json"
        $mockClientId = $response.client_id
        Write-Host "Mock client created with ID: $mockClientId" -ForegroundColor Green
        
        # If no specific client was specified, use this mock client
        if (-not $Client) {
            $Client = $mockClientId
            Write-Host "Using newly created mock client ID: $Client" -ForegroundColor Cyan
            # Add to pythonArgs if not already present
            if (-not ($pythonArgs -contains "--client")) {
                $pythonArgs += "--client", $Client
            }
        }
    } catch {
        Write-Host "Error creating mock client: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
    }
}

# Update permissions if requested
if (($GrantPermission -or $DenyPermission) -and $Client) {
    $permissionVal = if ($GrantPermission) { $true } else { $false }
    $permissionDesc = if ($GrantPermission) { "granted" } else { "denied" }
    
    Write-Host "$permissionDesc permission for client $Client..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    try {
        $body = @{
            clientId = $Client
            allowed = $permissionVal
            reason = "Set via PowerShell script"
        } | ConvertTo-Json
        
        $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Method POST -Uri "$Url/api/vscode/permission" -Body $body -ContentType "application/json"
        Write-Host "Permission successfully $permissionDesc for client $Client" -ForegroundColor Green
    } catch {
        Write-Host "Error setting permission: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
    }
}

Write-Host "PowerShell: Constructed pythonArgs before execution:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$pythonArgs | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  Arg: '$_'" -ForegroundColor Cyan }

# Run the Python script and capture its combined stdout and stderr
Write-Host "PowerShell: Executing Python script..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
$stdOutAndErr = (& python $pythonArgs 2>&1)
$exitCode = $LASTEXITCODE # Capture exit code immediately

if ($exitCode -ne 0) {
    Write-Host "Python script failed with exit code $exitCode." -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "Output from script (stdout/stderr):" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    $stdOutAndErr | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
    exit $exitCode
}

# If Python script was successful (exitCode is 0)
if ($List) {
    # Python script prints JSON to its stdout when --list is used.
    # All other prints (debug/log messages) go to its stderr.
    # $stdOutAndErr contains all lines, we need to find the JSON list.
    $jsonLine = $null
    foreach ($line in $stdOutAndErr) {
        if (-not ($line -is [string]) -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($line)) {
            continue
        }
        # Heuristic: JSON list starts with '[' and ends with ']'
        if ($line.TrimStart().StartsWith("[") -and $line.TrimEnd().EndsWith("]")) {
            try {
                # Attempt to parse. If it deserializes to a PowerShell array, it's likely our target.
                $parsedCandidate = $line | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
                if ($parsedCandidate -is [System.Array]) {
                    $jsonLine = $line
                    break # Found the JSON line
                }
            } catch {
                # Line was not parseable JSON or not an array, continue searching
            }
        }
    }

    if ($jsonLine) {
        try {
            $connectedClients = $jsonLine | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop
            Write-Host "Connected VS Code Clients:" -ForegroundColor Green
            if ($connectedClients.Count -gt 0) {
                $connectedClients | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "- $_" }
            } else {
                Write-Host "No clients reported by the script (empty list received)." -ForegroundColor Cyan
            }
            # Store in a variable for potential further use in the script
            $Global:ConnectedClientIDs = $connectedClients
            Write-Host "Client IDs are available in `$Global:ConnectedClientIDs" -ForegroundColor Magenta
        } catch {
            Write-Host "Failed to parse the identified JSON line ('$jsonLine') for client list." -ForegroundColor Red
            Write-Host "Specific Error: $($_.Exception.Message)" -ForegroundColor Red
            Write-Host "Full output from Python script was:" -ForegroundColor Yellow
            $stdOutAndErr | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
            exit 1 
        }
    } else {
        Write-Host "Could not find the JSON list in the Python script output." -ForegroundColor Yellow
        Write-Host "This may indicate an issue with the Python script or no clients connected and an unexpected output format." -ForegroundColor Yellow
        Write-Host "Full output from Python script was:" -ForegroundColor Yellow
        $stdOutAndErr | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
        # If the Python script is expected to always return a JSON array (e.g., "[]" for no clients),
        # then not finding $jsonLine might be considered an error.
        # For now, just a warning. If this state should be an error, add 'exit 1' here.
    }
} else {
    # Successful non-list command (e.g., branch change).
    # Python script's useful output (logs, success/failure messages for the operation) is on its stderr.
    # $stdOutAndErr contains everything (stdout and stderr from Python).
    Write-Host "Python script (non-list command) executed successfully (exit code 0)." -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "Full output from script (stdout/stderr):" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
    $stdOutAndErr | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ }
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Command-line tool to change branch in VS Code from the backend.
"""

import requests
import json
import time
import sys
import argparse
import traceback

# Helper to print dictionary nicely for logs
def format_dict_for_log(d):
    return json.dumps(d, indent=2, sort_keys=True)

def list_clients(base_url):
    """List all connected VS Code clients. Prints details to stderr, returns list of client IDs."""
    print("--- Entering list_clients --- ", file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"[list_clients] Base URL: {base_url}", file=sys.stderr)
    target_url = f"{base_url}/api/vscode/clients"
    print(f"[list_clients] Requesting client list from: {target_url}", file=sys.stderr)
    try:
        response = requests.get(target_url, timeout=10)
        print(f"[list_clients] Response status code: {response.status_code}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"[list_clients] Response headers: {format_dict_for_log(dict(response.headers))}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"[list_clients] Response body (raw text): {response.text}", file=sys.stderr)

        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"Error: [list_clients] API request failed. Status: {response.status_code}, Body: {response.text}", file=sys.stderr)
            print("--- Exiting list_clients (API error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
            return []
        
        try:
            clients_data = response.json()
            print(f"[list_clients] Parsed JSON response: {format_dict_for_log(clients_data)}", file=sys.stderr)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            print(f"Error: [list_clients] Failed to decode JSON response from API. Error: {str(e)}", file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"[list_clients] Raw response text that caused error: {response.text}", file=sys.stderr)
            print("--- Exiting list_clients (JSON decode error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
            return []

        clients = clients_data.get("clients", {})
        
        if not clients:
            print("[list_clients] No VS Code clients connected.", file=sys.stderr)
            print("--- Exiting list_clients (no clients) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
            return []
        
        connected_clients_ids = []
        print(f"[list_clients] Found {len(clients)} client(s):", file=sys.stderr)
        for client_id, client in clients.items():
            connection_status = "Connected" if client.get("connected") else "Disconnected"
            print(f"  ID: {client_id}", file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"    • Status: {connection_status}", file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"    • Workspace: {client.get('workspace_name')}", file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"    • Current Branch: {client.get('current_branch')}", file=sys.stderr)
            if client.get("connected"):
                connected_clients_ids.append(client_id)
        print(file=sys.stderr) # Extra newline for readability in stderr
        
        print(f"[list_clients] Returning connected client IDs: {connected_clients_ids}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("--- Exiting list_clients (success) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
        return connected_clients_ids
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout:
        print(f"Error: [list_clients] Timeout when fetching client list from {target_url}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("--- Exiting list_clients (timeout error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
        return []
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        print(f"Error: [list_clients] Request failed when fetching client list: {str(e)}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("--- Exiting list_clients (request error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
        return []
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        print(f"Error: [list_clients] Failed to decode JSON response from client list API: {str(e)}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"[list_clients] Response text was: {response.text if 'response' in locals() else 'N/A'}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("--- Exiting list_clients (JSON error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
        return []
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error: [list_clients] An unexpected error occurred: {str(e)}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Stack trace: {traceback.format_exc()}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("--- Exiting list_clients (unexpected error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
        return []

def change_branch(base_url, client_id, branch, commit=None):
    """Change branch for a specific VS Code client."""
    print("--- Entering change_branch --- ", file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"[change_branch] Parameters: base_url='{base_url}', client_id='{client_id}', branch='{branch}', commit='{commit}'", file=sys.stderr)
    try:
        checkout_data = {
            "branch": branch,
            "clientId": client_id,
            "commit": commit,
            "message": f"Branch change from backend to {branch}{f' at commit {commit}' if commit else ''}"
        }
        
        checkout_url = f"{base_url}/api/vscode/checkout"
        print(f"[change_branch] Attempting to POST checkout command to: {checkout_url}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"[change_branch] Checkout payload being sent: {format_dict_for_log(checkout_data)}", file=sys.stderr)
        
        response = requests.post(
            checkout_url, 
            json=checkout_data,
            timeout=15 # Increased timeout slightly
        )
        
        print(f"[change_branch] Checkout command response status code: {response.status_code}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"[change_branch] Checkout command response headers: {format_dict_for_log(dict(response.headers))}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"[change_branch] Checkout command response body (raw text): {response.text}", file=sys.stderr)

        if response.status_code in (200, 201):
            print("[change_branch] Checkout command sent successfully to backend.", file=sys.stderr)
            try:
                response_data = response.json()
                print(f"[change_branch] Parsed checkout response data: {format_dict_for_log(response_data)}", file=sys.stderr)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                print(f"[change_branch] Checkout response was not valid JSON, using raw text: '{response.text}'", file=sys.stderr)
            
            print("[change_branch] Waiting 5 seconds for VS Code to process the change and backend to update...", file=sys.stderr) # Increased wait time slightly
            time.sleep(5)
            
            verify_url = f"{base_url}/api/vscode/client/{client_id}"
            print(f"[change_branch] Verifying branch change by GETting client info from: {verify_url}", file=sys.stderr)
            client_info_response = requests.get(verify_url, timeout=10)

            print(f"[change_branch] Verification GET response status code: {client_info_response.status_code}", file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"[change_branch] Verification GET response headers: {format_dict_for_log(dict(client_info_response.headers))}", file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"[change_branch] Verification GET response body (raw text): {client_info_response.text}", file=sys.stderr)

            if client_info_response.status_code == 200:
                try:
                    client_data = client_info_response.json()
                    print(f"[change_branch] Parsed verification client data: {format_dict_for_log(client_data)}", file=sys.stderr)
                except json.JSONDecodeError as e_json_verify:
                    print(f"Error: [change_branch] Failed to decode JSON from verification response. Error: {str(e_json_verify)}", file=sys.stderr)
                    print(f"[change_branch] Raw verification response text: {client_info_response.text}", file=sys.stderr)
                    print("--- Exiting change_branch (verification JSON decode error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
                    return False

                new_branch = client_data.get("current_branch")
                current_commit = client_data.get("current_commit") # Assuming backend provides this
                # Also log other potentially relevant fields like 'workspace_name', 'connected_client_id'
                workspace_name = client_data.get("workspace_name")
                connected_client_id_from_api = client_data.get("connected_client_id") # This field name is an assumption

                print(f"[change_branch] Verification Details:", file=sys.stderr)
                print(f"  > Target Client ID: '{client_id}'", file=sys.stderr)
                print(f"  > Workspace Name (from API): '{workspace_name}'", file=sys.stderr)
                print(f"  > Connected Client ID (from API): '{connected_client_id_from_api}'", file=sys.stderr) # Log assumed field
                print(f"  > Expected Branch: '{branch}'", file=sys.stderr)
                print(f"  > Actual Branch (from API): '{new_branch}'", file=sys.stderr)
                print(f"  > Expected Commit (starts with): '{commit if commit else 'N/A'}'", file=sys.stderr)
                print(f"  > Actual Commit (from API): '{current_commit if current_commit else 'N/A'}'", file=sys.stderr)

                branch_match = (new_branch == branch)
                commit_match = True # Assume true if target commit is not specified
                if commit: 
                    commit_match = (current_commit and current_commit.startswith(commit))

                print(f"[change_branch] Branch Match Result: {branch_match}", file=sys.stderr)
                print(f"[change_branch] Commit Match Result (if applicable): {commit_match if commit else 'N/A'}", file=sys.stderr)

                if branch_match and (not commit or commit_match): # If commit is specified, it must match
                    success_message = f"Success: [change_branch] VS Code client '{client_id}' branch successfully changed to '{new_branch}'"
                    if commit:
                        success_message += f" and commit starts with '{commit}' (Actual: '{current_commit}')"
                    success_message += "."
                    print(success_message, file=sys.stderr)
                    print("--- Exiting change_branch (success) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
                    return True
                else:
                    print(f"Warning: [change_branch] Verification failed. Branch/commit did not match expected values for client '{client_id}'.", file=sys.stderr)
                    # Detailed reasons already printed above
                    print("  Possible reasons include:", file=sys.stderr)
                    print("  • Target branch/commit does not exist in the repository.", file=sys.stderr)
                    print("  • VS Code encountered an error during the git operation (check VS Code's Git output/logs).", file=sys.stderr)
                    print("  • Backend API did not reflect the change yet or reported stale data.", file=sys.stderr)
                    print("  • Discrepancy in commit hash (e.g. full vs. short, or different commit on the same branch if not specified).", file=sys.stderr)
                    print("--- Exiting change_branch (verification mismatch) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
                    return False
            else:
                print(f"Warning: [change_branch] Could not verify branch change. Verification GET request for client '{client_id}' failed. Status: {client_info_response.status_code}", file=sys.stderr)
                print(f"[change_branch] Raw verification response: {client_info_response.text}", file=sys.stderr)
                print("--- Exiting change_branch (verification HTTP error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
                return False
        else:
            print(f"Error: [change_branch] Backend failed to process checkout command for client '{client_id}'. Status: {response.status_code}", file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"[change_branch] Backend response: {response.text}", file=sys.stderr)
            print("--- Exiting change_branch (checkout command API error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
            return False
            
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e_timeout:
        print(f"Error: [change_branch] Timeout during operation: {str(e_timeout)}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Stack trace: {traceback.format_exc()}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("--- Exiting change_branch (timeout error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e_req:
        print(f"Error: [change_branch] Request failed: {str(e_req)}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Stack trace: {traceback.format_exc()}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("--- Exiting change_branch (request error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e_json_main:
        error_context = "an unknown API response"
        response_text_to_log = "N/A"
        if 'client_info_response' in locals() and client_info_response.status_code == 200: # Error was in parsing verification response
            error_context = "client info API verification response"
            response_text_to_log = client_info_response.text
        elif 'response' in locals() and response.status_code in (200,201): # Error was in parsing initial checkout response
            error_context = "checkout API command response"
            response_text_to_log = response.text
        print(f"Error: [change_branch] Failed to decode JSON from {error_context}: {str(e_json_main)}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"[change_branch] Raw response text that caused JSON error: {response_text_to_log}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Stack trace: {traceback.format_exc()}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("--- Exiting change_branch (JSON error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    except Exception as e_unexpected:
        print(f"Error: [change_branch] An unexpected error occurred: {str(e_unexpected)}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Stack trace: {traceback.format_exc()}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("--- Exiting change_branch (unexpected error) --- ", file=sys.stderr)
        return False

def main():
    """Main function."""
    print("=== Script Starting ===", file=sys.stderr)
    start_time = time.time()

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Change branch in VS Code via backend API.")
    parser.add_argument("--url", "-u", default="http://localhost:5000", help="Backend URL (default: http://localhost:5000)")
    parser.add_argument("--list", "-l", action="store_true", help="List connected clients (outputs JSON list of IDs to stdout, details to stderr)")
    parser.add_argument("--client", "-c", help="Client ID for branch change operation")
    parser.add_argument("--branch", "-b", help="Branch name to checkout")
    parser.add_argument("--commit", help="Commit hash (or short hash) to checkout (optional)")
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(f"[main] Parsed arguments: Namespace(url='{args.url}', list={args.list}, client='{args.client}', branch='{args.branch}', commit='{args.commit}')", file=sys.stderr)

    # Initial backend check (lightweight)
    print(f"[main] Performing initial backend check at {args.url}...", file=sys.stderr)
    try:
        response = requests.get(args.url, timeout=5) 
        if response.status_code == 200:
            print(f"[main] Backend check successful: {args.url} responded with {response.status_code}.", file=sys.stderr)
        else:
            print(f"Warning: [main] Backend at {args.url} responded with status: {response.status_code}. Body: {response.text[:200]}...", file=sys.stderr)
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout:
        print(f"Error: [main] Timeout connecting to the backend at {args.url}. Is it running and accessible?", file=sys.stderr)
        # For --list, list_clients will try again and handle its own errors.
        # For change_branch, it will also try and handle its errors.
        # No early exit here, let sub-commands try.
        print(f"Stack trace: {traceback.format_exc()}", file=sys.stderr)
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e_conn:
        print(f"Error: [main] Connection refused by backend at {args.url}. Is it running? Error: {e_conn}", file=sys.stderr)
        # If not --list, and backend is clearly down, might be good to exit early for other commands.
        if not args.list and not (args.client and args.branch):
            print("[main] Exiting due to connection error before specific command execution.", file=sys.stderr)
            print("=== Script Ended (Connection Error) ====", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1 # Critical error if backend is down and we need to change branch
        print(f"Stack trace: {traceback.format_exc()}", file=sys.stderr)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error: [main] Could not verify backend status at {args.url}: {str(e)}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Stack trace: {traceback.format_exc()}", file=sys.stderr)

    exit_code = 0
    if args.list:
        print("[main] Action: List clients", file=sys.stderr)
        clients_ids = list_clients(args.url)
        print(json.dumps(clients_ids)) # To stdout for PowerShell
        # list_clients prints its own success/failure to stderr
    
    elif args.client and args.branch:
        print(f"[main] Action: Change branch for client '{args.client}' to branch '{args.branch}' (commit: '{args.commit}')", file=sys.stderr)
        success = change_branch(args.url, args.client, args.branch, args.commit)
        if success:
            print("[main] Branch change operation reported success.", file=sys.stderr)
            exit_code = 0
        else:
            print("[main] Branch change operation reported failure.", file=sys.stderr)
            exit_code = 1
    
    else:
        print("[main] No specific action requested (e.g., --list or --client/--branch).", file=sys.stderr)
        print("[main] Printing help message and defaulting to verbose client list (to stderr).", file=sys.stderr)
        parser.print_help(sys.stderr)
        print("\n[main] Current connected clients (verbose to stderr):", file=sys.stderr)
        list_clients(args.url) # Verbose output to stderr for user info
        exit_code = 0 # Or 1 if this should be an error? For now, 0 as it's informational.
    
    end_time = time.time()
    print(f"[main] Total execution time: {end_time - start_time:.2f} seconds", file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"=== Script Ended (Exit Code: {exit_code}) ====", file=sys.stderr)
    return exit_code

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

--- FILE: C:\Users\urib9\projects\Hive mind\hive-mind\README.md ---
# Hive Mind

A GCP-based multi-agent engineering platform where users can spin up "AI product teams" composed of specialized LLM agents that collaborate to accomplish tasks.

## Overview

Hive Mind allows you to create teams of AI agents, each with a specific role (Planner, Architect, Coder, Tester, etc.), that work together in a shared environment to complete tasks. The system features:

- **Team Builder**: Create and configure teams with specific agent roles
- **Feedback Loop**: Agents iterate on tasks until success criteria are met
- **Cost Management**: Budget controls and model tier selection
- **Task Orchestration**: Smart task assignment based on complexity and budget
- **Agent Memory**: Long-term memory using vector embeddings for contextual assistance

## Features

- **Agent Framework**: Foundation for creating specialized agents with different roles
- **Feedback Loop**: Validation, iteration, and improvement cycle for tasks
- **Smart Tasking**: Tier-based model selection for cost efficiency
- **Cost Tracking**: Budget management and spending monitoring
- **Local Development**: Run the full system on your local machine with Docker
- **Memory System**: Vector-based memory for agents to recall past interactions and knowledge

## Architecture

The system consists of several key components:

- **Control Plane**: FastAPI service for managing teams, tasks, and agent communication
- **Agent SDK**: Base classes and utilities for building agents
- **Task Orchestrator**: Assigns tasks to agents based on complexity and budget
- **Cost Domain Manager**: Tracks and enforces budget constraints
- **Tools**: File operations, shell command execution, etc.
- **Vector Memory**: Stores and retrieves relevant context using semantic similarity

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- [Docker](https://www.docker.com/get-started) and Docker Compose
- Python 3.11+
- Node.js 18+

### Local Development

1. Clone the repository:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/your-org/hive-mind.git
   cd hive-mind
   ```

2. Set up environment variables:
   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   # Edit .env with your API keys and settings
   ```

3. Start the services with Docker Compose:
   ```bash
   docker-compose up -d
   ```

4. Access the services:
   - Control Plane API: http://localhost:8000
   - API Documentation: http://localhost:8000/docs
   - UI (when implemented): http://localhost:3000
   - RabbitMQ Management: http://localhost:15672
   - Prometheus: http://localhost:9090
   - Grafana: http://localhost:3001

## Project Structure

```
hive-mind/
├── agent-sdk/            # Agent framework and utilities
├── agents/               # Agent implementations
├── control-plane/        # FastAPI Control Plane service
├── cost-domain/          # Cost Domain Manager service
├── docker/               # Docker configurations
├── docs/                 # Documentation
├── infra/                # Terraform infrastructure code
├── task-orchestrator/    # Task Orchestrator & Tier Router
├── tests/                # Test suite
├── tools/                # Tool implementations
├── ui/                   # React/Tauri UI
├── docker-compose.yml    # Local development setup
├── requirements.txt      # Python dependencies
└── README.md             # This file
```

## Agent Roles

The system supports various agent roles, including:

- **Manager**: Orchestrates the team and handles communication
- **Planner**: Breaks down projects into tasks and creates strategic plans
- **Architect**: Designs system architecture and makes technology decisions
- **Coder**: Implements features according to specifications
- **Tester**: Verifies code quality and tests implementations

## Agent Memory System

Hive Mind includes a sophisticated memory system for agents:

- **Semantic Search**: Find relevant past information using vector embeddings
- **Contextual Retrieval**: Provide agents with context from previous interactions
- **Memory Types**: Store code snippets, task information, conversations, and more
- **Importance Scoring**: Prioritize memories based on relevance and importance
- **Integration**: Seamlessly incorporated into the agent workflow

Read more about the [Agent Memory System](docs/agent_memory_system.md).

--- FILE: C:\Users\urib9\projects\Hive mind\hive-mind\test-connection.py ---
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Test script to verify if the Hive Mind backend is accessible.
"""

import requests
import argparse
import sys

def test_connection(url):
    """Test if the backend is accessible at the given URL."""
    print(f"Testing connection to {url}...")
    
    try:
        # Test basic API connection
        response = requests.get(url, timeout=5)
        if response.status_code == 200:
            print("✅ Backend is accessible!")
            print(f"Response: {response.json()}")
            
            # Test VS Code API
            vscode_url = f"{url}/api/vscode/clients"
            print(f"\nTesting VS Code API at {vscode_url}...")
            
            try:
                response = requests.get(vscode_url, timeout=5)
                if response.status_code == 200:
                    print("✅ VS Code API is accessible!")
                    data = response.json()
                    client_count = len(data.get("clients", {}))
                    print(f"Found {client_count} connected VS Code clients")
                else:
                    print(f"❌ VS Code API returned status code: {response.status_code}")
            except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
                print(f"❌ Failed to connect to VS Code API: {str(e)}")
                
            return True
        else:
            print(f"❌ Backend returned status code: {response.status_code}")
            return False
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError:
        print("❌ Connection failed. Backend is not accessible.")
        print("Possible reasons:")
        print("  • The backend is not running")
        print("  • The URL is incorrect")
        print("  • Network issues or firewall blocking the connection")
        return False
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout:
        print("❌ Connection timed out. Backend might be running but is slow to respond.")
        return False
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ An error occurred: {str(e)}")
        return False

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Test connection to Hive Mind backend.")
    parser.add_argument("--url", "-u", default="http://localhost:5000", 
                      help="Backend URL (default: http://localhost:5000)")
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    success = test_connection(args.url)
    return 0 if success else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main()) 


--- FILE: C:\Users\urib9\projects\Hive mind\hive-mind\test-vscode-api.ps1 ---
# PowerShell script to test VS Code API endpoints

param (
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [string]$BaseUrl = "http://localhost:5000",
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [switch]$CreateMockClient,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [switch]$ListClients,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [string]$GetClient,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [string]$ClientId,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [string]$Branch,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [string]$Commit,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [switch]$GrantPermission,
    
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)]
    [switch]$DenyPermission
)

Write-Host "VS Code API Test Script" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "======================" -ForegroundColor Cyan

# Create a mock client for testing
if ($CreateMockClient) {
    Write-Host "Creating mock client..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    try {
        $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Method POST -Uri "$BaseUrl/api/vscode/mock" -ContentType "application/json"
        Write-Host "Mock client created successfully:" -ForegroundColor Green
        $response | ConvertTo-Json
        $Global:LastCreatedClientId = $response.client_id
        Write-Host "Client ID stored in `$Global:LastCreatedClientId: $($Global:LastCreatedClientId)" -ForegroundColor Magenta
    }
    catch {
        Write-Host "Error creating mock client: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
    }
}

# List all clients
if ($ListClients) {
    Write-Host "Listing all VS Code clients..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    try {
        $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Method GET -Uri "$BaseUrl/api/vscode/clients" -ContentType "application/json"
        Write-Host "Clients retrieved successfully:" -ForegroundColor Green
        $response | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
        $clientsArray = @()
        foreach ($key in $response.clients.PSObject.Properties.Name) {
            $clientsArray += [PSCustomObject]@{
                ClientId = $key
                WorkspaceName = $response.clients.$key.workspace_name
                CurrentBranch = $response.clients.$key.current_branch
                Connected = $response.clients.$key.connected
                Permission = $response.clients.$key.permission
            }
        }
        $Global:VSCodeClients = $clientsArray
        Write-Host "Clients data stored in `$Global:VSCodeClients" -ForegroundColor Magenta
    }
    catch {
        Write-Host "Error listing clients: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
    }
}

# Get information about a specific client
if ($GetClient) {
    Write-Host "Getting information for client: $GetClient" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    try {
        $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Method GET -Uri "$BaseUrl/api/vscode/client/$GetClient" -ContentType "application/json"
        Write-Host "Client information retrieved successfully:" -ForegroundColor Green
        $response | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
        $Global:VSCodeClientInfo = $response
        Write-Host "Client info stored in `$Global:VSCodeClientInfo" -ForegroundColor Magenta
    }
    catch {
        Write-Host "Error getting client info: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
    }
}

# Grant permission to a client
if ($GrantPermission -and $ClientId) {
    Write-Host "Granting permission to client: $ClientId" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    try {
        $body = @{
            clientId = $ClientId
            allowed = $true
            reason = "Granted via test script"
        } | ConvertTo-Json
        
        $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Method POST -Uri "$BaseUrl/api/vscode/permission" -Body $body -ContentType "application/json"
        Write-Host "Permission granted successfully:" -ForegroundColor Green
        $response | ConvertTo-Json
    }
    catch {
        Write-Host "Error granting permission: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
    }
}

# Deny permission to a client
if ($DenyPermission -and $ClientId) {
    Write-Host "Denying permission to client: $ClientId" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    try {
        $body = @{
            clientId = $ClientId
            allowed = $false
            reason = "Denied via test script"
        } | ConvertTo-Json
        
        $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Method POST -Uri "$BaseUrl/api/vscode/permission" -Body $body -ContentType "application/json"
        Write-Host "Permission denied successfully:" -ForegroundColor Green
        $response | ConvertTo-Json
    }
    catch {
        Write-Host "Error denying permission: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
    }
}

# Change branch for a client
if ($ClientId -and $Branch) {
    Write-Host "Changing branch for client: $ClientId to $Branch" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    
    $body = @{
        clientId = $ClientId
        branch = $Branch
    }
    
    if ($Commit) {
        $body.commit = $Commit
        Write-Host "Including commit: $Commit" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    }
    
    try {
        $bodyJson = $body | ConvertTo-Json
        $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Method POST -Uri "$BaseUrl/api/vscode/checkout" -Body $bodyJson -ContentType "application/json"
        Write-Host "Branch change request processed successfully:" -ForegroundColor Green
        $response | ConvertTo-Json
    }
    catch {
        Write-Host "Error changing branch: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
        if ($_.Exception.Response) {
            try {
                $responseBody = $_.Exception.Response.GetResponseStream()
                $reader = New-Object System.IO.StreamReader($responseBody)
                $responseText = $reader.ReadToEnd()
                Write-Host "Response body: $responseText" -ForegroundColor Red
            }
            catch {
                Write-Host "Could not read error response: $_" -ForegroundColor Red
            }
        }
    }
}

"""

"""

import requests
import json
import time
import sys

def test_vscode_control():
    """Test if the backend can control VS Code."""
    base_url = "http://localhost:5000"
    
    print("\n=== Testing Hive Mind VS Code Control ===\n")
    
    # Step 1: Check if the API is running
    try:
        print("1. Checking if the backend is running...")
        response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/")
        if response.status_code == 200:
            print("✅ Backend is running!")
        else:
            print(f"❌ Backend responded with status code: {response.status_code}")
            return False
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError:
        print("❌ Failed to connect to the backend. Make sure it's running on http://localhost:5000")
        return False
    
    # Step 2: Get list of connected VS Code clients
    print("\n2. Checking for connected VS Code clients...")
    try:
        response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/api/vscode/clients")
        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"❌ Failed to get client list: {response.status_code}")
            return False
        
        clients_data = response.json()
        clients = clients_data.get("clients", {})
        
        if not clients:
            print("❌ No VS Code clients connected. Make sure VS Code is running with the extension installed")
            return False
        
        print(f"✅ Found {len(clients)} connected client(s)!")
        for client_id, client in clients.items():
            connection_status = "Connected" if client.get("connected") else "Disconnected"
            print(f"   • Client ID: {client_id[:8]}... ({connection_status})")
            print(f"     Workspace: {client.get('workspace_name')}")
            print(f"     Current Branch: {client.get('current_branch')}")
        
        # Get the first client ID
        client_id = next(iter(clients.keys()))
        workspace_name = clients[client_id].get("workspace_name")
        current_branch = clients[client_id].get("current_branch")
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Error getting clients: {str(e)}")
        return False
    
    # Step 3: Try to change branch
    print(f"\n3. Attempting to change branch for client {client_id[:8]}...")
    
    # Determine target branch (different from current)
    target_branch = "main" if current_branch != "main" else "develop"
    
    try:
        checkout_data = {
            "branch": target_branch,
            "clientId": client_id,
            "message": "Test branch switch from backend"
        }
        
        response = requests.post(
            f"{base_url}/api/vscode/checkout", 
            json=checkout_data
        )
        
        if response.status_code in (200, 201):
            print(f"✅ Sent command to switch to branch '{target_branch}'")
            print(f"   Response: {response.json()}")
            
            # Wait a bit and check if branch was changed
            print("\n   Waiting 3 seconds for VS Code to process the change...")
            time.sleep(3)
            
            response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/api/vscode/client/{client_id}")
            if response.status_code == 200:
                client_data = response.json()
                new_branch = client_data.get("current_branch")
                
                if new_branch == target_branch:
                    print(f"✅ SUCCESS! Branch successfully changed to '{new_branch}'")
                    print("\n=== VS Code control is working correctly! ===")
                    return True
                else:
                    print(f"❌ Branch didn't change. Still on '{new_branch}'")
                    print("   This might be because:")
                    print("   • The target branch doesn't exist in the repository")
                    print("   • VS Code couldn't execute the Git command")
                    print("   • The backend didn't properly track the change")
        else:
            print(f"❌ Failed to send checkout command: {response.status_code}")
            print(f"   Response: {response.text}")
            
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Error sending checkout command: {str(e)}")
    
    print("\n=== Test completed with errors ===")
    return False

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_vscode_control()

# VS Code Git Branch Control System

This guide explains how to use the Hive Mind VS Code extension to control the Git branch context from your backend.

## Setup Steps

1. **Install the VS Code Extension:**
   ```powershell
   # Navigate to the extension directory
   cd vscode-hive-mind-extension
   
   # Run the installation script
   .\install.ps1
   ```

2. **Start the Backend Service:**
   ```powershell
   # Navigate to the hive-mind directory
   cd hive-mind
   
   # Start the backend service
   docker-compose up -d hive-mind-backend
   ```

3. **Reload VS Code:**
   - In VS Code, press `Ctrl+Shift+P` and run "Developer: Reload Window"
   - Make sure you have a Git repository open in VS Code

## Connecting to the Backend

The extension will attempt to auto-connect to the default backend URL (http://localhost:5000) when VS Code starts. You have two ways to manually control the connection:

1. **Standard Connection:**
   - Press `Ctrl+Shift+P` to open the Command Palette
   - Type "Hive Mind: Connect to Backend" and press Enter
   - This connects to the default backend URL or the last saved URL

2. **Custom Connection:**
   - Press `Ctrl+Shift+P` to open the Command Palette
   - Type "Hive Mind: Connect to Custom Backend URL" and press Enter
   - Enter the backend URL (e.g., http://192.168.1.100:5000)
   - This URL will be saved for future connections

3. **Disconnecting:**
   - Press `Ctrl+Shift+P` to open the Command Palette
   - Type "Hive Mind: Disconnect from Backend" and press Enter

4. **Checking Status:**
   - Click on the Hive Mind indicator in the status bar, or
   - Press `Ctrl+Shift+P` and type "Hive Mind: Show Connection Status"

## Testing the Connection

1. **Check if VS Code is connected:**
   ```powershell
   # Navigate to the hive-mind directory
   cd hive-mind
   
   # List connected VS Code clients
   .\change-vscode-branch.ps1 -List
   ```

   If you see "No VS Code clients connected", try the following:
   - Make sure VS Code is open with a Git repository
   - Use the Command Palette to connect manually (as described above)
   - Check the VS Code extension is installed (look for "Hive Mind" in the status bar)
   - Try connecting to a custom URL if your backend is running on a different machine

2. **Change Branch in VS Code:**
   - Once your client is connected, note the client ID from the list
   - Run the following command to change the branch:
   ```powershell
   .\change-vscode-branch.ps1 -Client "your-client-id" -Branch "main"
   ```

   Replace `your-client-id` with the actual client ID from the list, and `main` with the branch you want to switch to.

## Using in Your Backend Code

To control VS Code from your backend code, use the following:

```python
import requests

def change_vs_code_branch(client_id, branch, commit=None):
    """Change the branch in a connected VS Code client."""
    checkout_data = {
        "branch": branch,
        "clientId": client_id,
        "commit": commit,
        "message": f"Switching to {branch}"
    }
    
    response = requests.post(
        "http://localhost:5000/api/vscode/checkout", 
        json=checkout_data
    )
    
    return response.json()

# Example usage
client_id = "get-this-from-listing-clients"
change_vs_code_branch(client_id, "develop")
```

## Troubleshooting

1. **VS Code doesn't connect to backend:**
   - Make sure the backend is running: `docker ps | findstr hive-mind-backend`
   - Check backend logs: `docker logs hive-mind-hive-mind-backend-1`
   - Try connecting to a custom URL using the Command Palette
   - Check your network firewall if connecting to a remote machine

2. **Branch change doesn't work:**
   - Make sure the branch exists in your Git repository
   - Check if you have uncommitted changes that prevent branch switching
   - Look at the VS Code Git panel for any error messages

3. **Extension doesn't show in VS Code:**
   - Verify extension installation path: `%USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\vscode-hive-mind-extension`
   - Check VS Code extensions panel to see if it's listed
   - Try reinstalling: `.\vscode-hive-mind-extension\install.ps1`

## Connection Across Machines

If your backend runs on a different machine than VS Code:

1. **On the backend machine:**
   - Make sure the backend listens on all interfaces (0.0.0.0) not just localhost
   - Ensure your firewall allows connections on port 5000
   - Find your machine's IP address using `ipconfig` (Windows) or `ifconfig` (Linux/macOS)

2. **In VS Code:**
   - Use the "Connect to Custom Backend URL" command
   - Enter the IP address of the backend machine (e.g., http://192.168.1.100:5000)

## Branch Control API

The backend API provides these endpoints:

- `GET /api/vscode/clients` - List all connected VS Code clients
- `GET /api/vscode/client/{client_id}` - Get information about a specific client
- `POST /api/vscode/checkout` - Change branch for a specific client
- `POST /api/vscode/register` - Register a new VS Code client (used by the extension)

# VS Code Permissions System

This document describes the permissions system for controlling VS Code clients from the Hive Mind backend.

## Overview

The Hive Mind system can control VS Code clients by changing their Git branches and commits. To ensure this is done securely and with user consent, a permissions system has been implemented.

## How Permissions Work

1. When a VS Code client registers with the backend, it starts with permissions disabled by default
2. Before performing operations like changing branches, the backend checks if the client has granted permission
3. If permission has not been granted, the backend will request it from the client
4. The user can grant or deny permission via a dialog in VS Code
5. Permission status is stored on the backend and persists until explicitly changed

## Permission Workflows

### Automatic Permission Request

When the backend attempts to change a branch for a client without permission:

1. The backend sends a `request-permission` event to the client
2. VS Code shows a dialog asking the user to grant or deny permission
3. The user's choice is sent back to the backend via a `permission-response` event
4. If granted, the backend will automatically retry the operation

### Manual Permission Management

Permissions can be managed manually using the following methods:

1. **VS Code Extension Commands**:
   - `hivemind.grantPermission` - Grant permission to the backend
   - `hivemind.denyPermission` - Deny permission to the backend

2. **Backend API Endpoints**:
   - `POST /api/vscode/permission` - Set permission for a specific client

## API Reference

### Backend API Endpoints

#### List VS Code Clients

```
GET /api/vscode/clients
```

Returns a list of all registered VS Code clients, including their permission status.

#### Get Client Information

```
GET /api/vscode/client/{client_id}
```

Returns detailed information about a specific client, including permission status.

#### Set Permission

```
POST /api/vscode/permission
```

Body:
```json
{
  "clientId": "client-id-here",
  "allowed": true,
  "reason": "Optional reason for the permission change"
}
```

#### Change Branch

```
POST /api/vscode/checkout
```

Body:
```json
{
  "clientId": "client-id-here",
  "branch": "branch-name",
  "commit": "optional-commit-hash",
  "message": "Optional message explaining the change"
}
```

Response codes:
- 200: Command sent successfully
- 403: Permission denied
- 404: Client not found
- 400: Client not connected
- 500: Server error

### Socket.IO Events

#### request-permission (Server to Client)

Sent when the backend needs permission to perform an operation.

```javascript
{
  "requestType": "branch-checkout",
  "details": {
    "branch": "main",
    "commit": "commit-hash",
    "message": "Reason for the checkout"
  }
}
```

#### permission-response (Client to Server)

Sent by the client in response to a permission request.

```javascript
{
  "granted": true,
  "requestType": "branch-checkout",
  "reason": "User granted permission via VS Code UI"
}
```

## Testing with Mock Clients

For testing purposes, you can create mock clients using:

```
POST /api/vscode/mock
```

This creates a mock client with permission already granted.

## Debugging Permission Issues

If a branch change fails due to permission issues, check:

1. The client's current permission status using the `/api/vscode/client/{client_id}` endpoint
2. The VS Code extension logs for any permission request events
3. The backend logs for permission-related messages

You can use the `test-vscode-api.ps1` script to test and debug permission functionality:

```powershell
# Create a mock client
.\test-vscode-api.ps1 -CreateMockClient

# List all clients and their permission status
.\test-vscode-api.ps1 -ListClients

# Grant permission to a specific client
.\test-vscode-api.ps1 -ClientId "client-id-here" -GrantPermission

# Deny permission to a specific client
.\test-vscode-api.ps1 -ClientId "client-id-here" -DenyPermission
```

# Work Mode Implementation

This document summarizes the changes made to implement the Work Mode feature in the Hive Mind system.

## Overview

The Work Mode feature has been implemented to establish real-time collaboration between VS Code users and the Hive Mind agent system. This feature enables:

1. Permission prompting at the beginning of a VS Code session
2. Tracking and processing of file changes made by users in VS Code
3. Integration of user changes with the agent system's common knowledge
4. Creating new tasks based on user changes when appropriate
5. Real-time communication between VS Code users and agents

## Changes Made

### VS Code Extension

1. Enhanced `extension.js`:
   - Added file change tracking using VS Code's FileSystemWatcher
   - Implemented debounced change batching to avoid overwhelming the backend
   - Added permission prompting at the start of each session
   - Added functions for sending/receiving messages to/from the backend

2. Updated `package.json`:
   - Added new commands for managing permissions
   - Added activation on startup and Git repository detection
   - Added new configuration options for controlling tracking features

### Backend VS Code Controller

1. Enhanced `vscode_controller.py`:
   - Added file change handling through new socket.io events
   - Implemented file change storage and tracking
   - Added a function to send messages to VS Code clients
   - Added integration hooks for the agent system

### Agent System

1. Created `vscode_change_handler.py`:
   - Processes file changes from VS Code clients
   - Determines if changes relate to existing tasks
   - Creates summaries of changes for agent consumption
   - Sends responses back to VS Code clients

2. Created/updated `manager_agent.py`:
   - Integrated with the VS Code change handler
   - Added logic to evaluate if changes warrant creating new tasks
   - Added message handling for user communications
   - Manages the relationship between VS Code clients and tasks

3. Updated `main.py`:
   - Added initialization of the manager agent
   - Connected the manager agent to the VS Code controller
   - Added startup/shutdown handlers for proper lifecycle management

### UI Components

1. Created `WorkMode.tsx`:
   - Displays connected VS Code clients
   - Shows real-time file changes
   - Provides a messaging interface
   - Visualizes agent-client interactions

2. Updated `Dashboard.tsx`:
   - Added a new tab for the Work Mode component
   - Improved layout to better integrate the new feature
   - Added state management for the active tab

3. Added CSS styles in `Dashboard.css`:
   - Styled the Work Mode component
   - Added dark mode support
   - Improved overall dashboard layout and navigation

### Documentation

1. Created `WORK_MODE.md`:
   - Documented the feature's components and functionality
   - Provided instructions for setup and use
   - Included troubleshooting information
   - Detailed the API endpoints and events

2. Created `WORK_MODE_IMPLEMENTATION.md`:
   - Summarized the changes made
   - Provided insights into the implementation approach
   - Listed potential future improvements

## Implementation Approach

The implementation follows these key principles:

1. **Backend-Driven**: The permission system is managed by the backend, which maintains authority over client connections and permissions.

2. **Real-Time Communication**: Socket.IO provides real-time bidirectional communication between VS Code clients and the backend.

3. **Debounced Tracking**: File changes are batched and debounced to avoid overwhelming the system with events.

4. **Agent Integration**: File changes are processed through the manager agent, which determines appropriate actions.

5. **UI Integration**: The Work Mode UI provides visibility into the system's operation and enables user communication.

## Future Improvements

Potential future improvements include:

1. **Enhanced Change Analysis**: Implement more sophisticated analysis of file changes to better determine their significance.

2. **Contextual Responses**: Provide more context-aware responses from agents based on the specific changes.

3. **Collaborative Editing**: Enable multiple VS Code clients to work on the same task with agent coordination.

4. **History and Analytics**: Add more detailed history views and analytics for VS Code usage patterns.

5. **Selective Change Tracking**: Allow users to specify which files or directories should be tracked.

## Conclusion

The Work Mode feature successfully bridges the gap between VS Code users and the Hive Mind agent system, enabling real-time collaboration and feedback. This implementation lays the groundwork for more sophisticated agent-assisted development workflows in the future.
