    async def run_tests_on_branch(self, branch_name: str, task_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Run tests on a specific branch
        
        Args:
            branch_name: Branch to test
            task_id: Task identifier
            
        Returns:
            Test results
        """
        logger.info(f"Running tests on branch {branch_name} for task {task_id}")
        
        # Check if branch exists
        branch_node = self.branch_tree.get_branch(branch_name)
        if not branch_node:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": f"Branch '{branch_name}' not found",
                "details": "Cannot run tests on non-existent branch"
            }
            
        # Execute CI/CD workflow for testing
        test_result = await self.run_ci_cd_workflow(branch_name, "HEAD")
        
        # Parse result
        if test_result.get("status") == "success":
            # Extract test step results
            test_steps = [step for step in test_result.get("steps", []) if step.get("name") == "test"]
            if test_steps and test_steps[0].get("status") == "success":
                return {
                    "status": "success",
                    "branch": branch_name,
                    "task_id": task_id,
                    "details": f"All tests passed on branch {branch_name}",
                    "timestamp": asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
                }
            else:
                return {
                    "status": "failure",
                    "branch": branch_name,
                    "task_id": task_id,
                    "details": f"Tests failed on branch {branch_name}",
                    "timestamp": asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
                }
        else:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "branch": branch_name,
                "task_id": task_id,
                "message": test_result.get("message", "Unknown error"),
                "details": "CI/CD workflow failed to run tests",
                "timestamp": asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
            }
            
    async def _merge_branches(self, source_branch: str, target_branch: str, task_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Merge source branch into target branch
        
        Args:
            source_branch: Source branch name
            target_branch: Target branch name
            task_id: Task identifier
            
        Returns:
            Merge result
        """
        logger.info(f"Merging {source_branch} into {target_branch} for task {task_id}")
        
        try:
            # Use git extension to perform merge
            result = self.git_extension.git.merge_branches(
                source_branch=source_branch,
                target_branch=target_branch,
                commit_message=f"Merge {source_branch} into {target_branch} for task {task_id}"
            )
            
            if result.get("status") != "success":
                return {
                    "status": "error",
                    "message": result.get("message", "Unknown merge error"),
                    "source_branch": source_branch,
                    "target_branch": target_branch
                }
                
            # Check if we should deploy after merging to main branches
            if target_branch in ["main", "master"] and self.ci_cd_config["auto_deploy"]:
                # Auto-deploy to production
                deploy_result = await self.deploy_to_environment("production", target_branch)
                result["deployment"] = deploy_result
            elif target_branch == "develop" and "staging" in self.ci_cd_config["environments"] and self.ci_cd_config["auto_deploy"]:
                # Auto-deploy to staging
                deploy_result = await self.deploy_to_environment("staging", target_branch)
                result["deployment"] = deploy_result
                
            return {
                "status": "success",
                "source_branch": source_branch,
                "target_branch": target_branch,
                "commits": result.get("commits", []),
                "files_changed": result.get("files_changed", []),
                "timestamp": asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
            }
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Exception merging branches: {str(e)}")
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": str(e),
                "source_branch": source_branch,
                "target_branch": target_branch
            }
            
    async def deploy_to_environment(self, environment: str, branch: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Deploy a branch to a specific environment
        
        Args:
            environment: Environment to deploy to
            branch: Branch to deploy
            
        Returns:
            Deployment result
        """
        if environment not in self.ci_cd_config["environments"]:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": f"Environment '{environment}' not configured",
                "environment": environment,
                "branch": branch
            }
            
        if environment not in self.ci_cd_config["deploy_commands"]:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": f"No deployment command for environment '{environment}'",
                "environment": environment,
                "branch": branch
            }
            
        logger.info(f"Deploying {branch} to {environment}")
        
        # Simulate deployment
        return {
            "status": "success",
            "environment": environment,
            "branch": branch,
            "command": self.ci_cd_config["deploy_commands"][environment],
            "timestamp": asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
        }

    def _get_next_steps_guidance(self, branch_name: str, test_status: str, task_id: str) -> str:
        """Generate guidance for next steps based on branch and test status"""
        if test_status == "failed":
            return """
Next Steps:
1. Fix the failing tests
2. Commit your changes
3. Tests will run automatically on your next commit
"""
        elif test_status == "passed" or test_status == "skipped":
            return """
Next Steps:
1. If your task is complete, request a merge with:
   - Send a message of type 'merge_request'
   - Include source_branch, target_branch, and task_id

2. If you need to make more changes:
   - Continue working on your branch
   - Commit changes as needed
"""
        else:
            return """
Next Steps:
1. Continue working on your branch
2. Commit changes as needed
"""

    def _save_branch_tree(self) -> None:
        """Save branch tree to persistent storage"""
        try:
            # Ensure directory exists
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.branch_tree_file), exist_ok=True)
            
            # Save to file
            self.branch_tree.save_to_file(self.branch_tree_file)
            logger.info(f"Saved branch tree to {self.branch_tree_file}")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to save branch tree: {str(e)}")
        
    async def _handle_strategy_request(self, message: Message) -> Message:
        """Handle a Git branching strategy request"""
        # Extract strategy from message
        strategy = self._extract_branching_strategy(message.content)
        
        # Check if this is a branch visualization request
        if "visualize" in message.content.lower() or "show branches" in message.content.lower():
            return await self._visualize_branch_tree(message)
            
        if not strategy:
            # Default to current strategy
            strategy = self.git_extension.git.branch_strategy
            
        # Check with manager to update strategy
        try:
            # Notify manager about strategy decision
            strategy_message = await self.send_message(
                recipients=["manager"],
                content=f"I recommend using the {strategy} branching strategy for this project. Please confirm.",
                context_tags=["#git_strategy", "#recommendation"],
                message_type="strategy_recommendation",
                thread_id=message.thread_id,
                requires_response=True
            )
            
            # In a real implementation, we'd wait for the manager's response
            # For demo purposes, we'll assume it's approved
            
            # Update our own strategy
            self.git_extension.git.branch_strategy = strategy
            
            # Reset branch tree with new strategy
            self.branch_tree = BranchTree(strategy)
            self._save_branch_tree()
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Could not coordinate with manager: {str(e)}")
        
        # Generate strategy documentation
        strategy_doc = await self.execute_with_git(
            self.create_strategy_documentation,
            strategy=strategy,
            commit_message=f"DevOps: Document {strategy} branching strategy"
        )
        
        # Prepare response
        response_content = f"""
I've established the {strategy} branching strategy for this project.

Key aspects of this strategy:
{strategy_doc['description']}

Branch naming conventions:
{strategy_doc['naming_conventions']}

Workflow:
{strategy_doc['workflow']}

The branch tree has been initialized with the {strategy} structure.
The strategy documentation has been committed to the repository.
"""

        return await self.send_message(
            recipients=[message.sender],
            content=response_content,
            context_tags=message.context_tags + ["#git_strategy"],
            message_type="strategy_result",
            thread_id=message.thread_id
        )
    
    async def _visualize_branch_tree(self, message: Message) -> Message:
        """Generate a visualization of the branch tree structure"""
        # Create a text-based tree visualization
        tree_text = self._generate_tree_visualization()
        
        # Current active branches by agent
        agent_branches_text = "### Active Branches by Agent\n"
        for agent_id, branches in self.agent_branches.items():
            active_branches = [b for b in branches 
                             if self.branch_tree.get_branch(b) and 
                                self.branch_tree.get_branch(b).status == "active"]
            if active_branches:
                agent_branches_text += f"- **{agent_id}**: {', '.join(active_branches)}\n"
                
        # Tasks and their branches
        task_branches_text = "### Tasks and Branches\n"
        for task_id, branch_name in self.task_branches.items():
            branch = self.branch_tree.get_branch(branch_name)
            if branch and branch.status == "active":
                task_branches_text += f"- **Task {task_id}**: {branch_name} ({branch.branch_type})\n"
                
        # Recent branch history
        history_text = "### Recent Branch Activity\n"
        recent_history = self.branch_history[-10:] if self.branch_history else []
        for entry in recent_history:
            action = entry.get("action", "")
            if action == "create":
                history_text += f"- {entry.get('timestamp', '').split('T')[0]} | **Created** branch '{entry.get('branch', '')}' from '{entry.get('parent', '')}'\n"
            elif action == "commit":
                history_text += f"- {entry.get('timestamp', '').split('T')[0]} | **Commit** to '{entry.get('branch', '')}' by {entry.get('agent_id', '')}\n"
            elif action == "merge":
                history_text += f"- {entry.get('timestamp', '').split('T')[0]} | **Merged** '{entry.get('source_branch', '')}' into '{entry.get('target_branch', '')}'\n"
                
        # Complete response
        response_content = f"""
# Branch Tree Visualization

{tree_text}

{agent_branches_text}

{task_branches_text}

{history_text}

The branch tree uses the **{self.branch_tree.strategy}** branching strategy.
"""

        return await self.send_message(
            recipients=[message.sender],
            content=response_content,
            context_tags=message.context_tags + ["#git_strategy", "#visualization"],
            message_type="branch_visualization",
            thread_id=message.thread_id
        )
        
    def _generate_tree_visualization(self) -> str:
        """Generate a text-based visualization of the branch tree"""
        if not self.branch_tree.root:
            return "No branches found."
            
        lines = []
        
        def _draw_tree(node, prefix="", is_last=True, level=0):
            # Define branch status indicators
            status_icons = {
                "active": "🟢",
                "merged": "🔵",
                "abandoned": "🔴"
            }
            
            # Branch node connector style
            connector = "└── " if is_last else "├── "
            
            # Add line for this node
            status = status_icons.get(node.status, "⚪")
            test_status = "✅" if node.tested else "❓"
            
            # Format line based on branch type
            if node.branch_type == "main" or node.branch_type == "develop":
                line = f"{prefix}{connector}**{node.name}** {status} {test_status}"
            else:
                agent_info = f" [{node.agent_id}]" if node.agent_id else ""
                task_info = f" (Task: {node.task_id})" if node.task_id else ""
                line = f"{prefix}{connector}{node.name} {status} {test_status}{agent_info}{task_info}"
                
            lines.append(line)
            
            # Prepare prefix for children
            child_prefix = prefix + ("    " if is_last else "│   ")
            
            # Process children
            children = node.children
            for i, child in enumerate(children):
                _draw_tree(child, child_prefix, i == len(children) - 1, level + 1)
                
        # Start with the root node
        _draw_tree(self.branch_tree.root)
        
        return "\n".join(lines)
    
    async def _register_external_commit(self, 
                              branch_name: str,
                              agent_id: str,
                              commit_hash: str,
                              commit_message: str,
                              files_changed: List[str],
                              task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Register a commit from an external agent
        
        Args:
            branch_name: Branch that was committed to
            agent_id: ID of the agent that made the commit
            commit_hash: Commit hash
            commit_message: Commit message
            files_changed: List of files that were changed
            task_id: Optional task ID
            
        Returns:
            Registration result
        """
        # Validate branch exists
        branch_node = self.branch_tree.get_branch(branch_name)
        if not branch_node:
            # This is a new branch we don't know about yet
            # Try to determine parent based on git history
            try:
                parent_info = self.git_extension.git.get_branch_parent(branch_name)
                if parent_info.get("status") == "success" and parent_info.get("parent_branch"):
                    parent_branch = parent_info.get("parent_branch")
                    
                    # Determine branch type from name
                    if branch_name.startswith("feature/"):
                        branch_type = "feature"
                    elif branch_name.startswith("bugfix/"):
                        branch_type = "bugfix"
                    elif branch_name.startswith("hotfix/"):
                        branch_type = "hotfix"
                    elif branch_name.startswith("release/"):
                        branch_type = "release"
                    else:
                        branch_type = "feature"  # Default
                    
                    # Add to branch tree
                    branch_node = self.branch_tree.add_branch(
                        name=branch_name,
                        parent_name=parent_branch,
                        branch_type=branch_type,
                        task_id=task_id,
                        agent_id=agent_id
                    )
                    
                    # Update mappings
                    if agent_id not in self.agent_branches:
                        self.agent_branches[agent_id] = set()
                    self.agent_branches[agent_id].add(branch_name)
                    
                    if task_id:
                        self.task_branches[task_id] = branch_name
                        
                    # Save branch tree
                    self._save_branch_tree()
                else:
                    logger.warning(f"Could not determine parent for unknown branch {branch_name}")
                    return {
                        "status": "error",
                        "message": f"Branch {branch_name} not found in branch tree and could not determine parent.",
                        "branch_name": branch_name,
                        "agent_id": agent_id
                    }
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Error determining parent for branch {branch_name}: {str(e)}")
                return {
                    "status": "error",
                    "message": f"Branch {branch_name} not found in branch tree: {str(e)}",
                    "branch_name": branch_name,
                    "agent_id": agent_id
                }
        
        # Update branch history
        self.branch_history.append({
            "action": "commit",
            "branch": branch_name,
            "commit_hash": commit_hash,
            "agent_id": agent_id,
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "message": commit_message,
            "files_changed": files_changed,
            "task_id": task_id
        })
        
        # Check if we need to run tests
        if self.ci_cd_config["run_tests"] and self.ci_cd_config["enabled"]:
            # Running tests on auto-commit is optional depending on CI/CD settings
            if self.ci_cd_config.get("test_on_commit", True):
                # Run tests asynchronously (don't wait for results here)
                asyncio.create_task(self.run_tests_on_branch(branch_name, task_id or "unknown"))
        
        return {
            "status": "success",
            "message": f"Registered commit {commit_hash[:7]} on branch {branch_name}",
            "branch_name": branch_name,
            "agent_id": agent_id,
            "run_tests": self.ci_cd_config["run_tests"] and self.ci_cd_config.get("test_on_commit", True)
        }
        
    async def setup_agent_auto_commit_hook(self, agent_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Set up auto-commit hook for an agent
        
        Args:
            agent_id: Agent ID to set up hook for
            
        Returns:
            Setup result
        """
        # This would typically be implemented by injecting a post-edit hook
        # into the agent's workflow that calls back to this agent
        
        # For now, we'll just return success and assume each agent will notify us
        return {
            "status": "success",
            "message": f"Auto-commit hook set up for agent {agent_id}",
            "agent_id": agent_id
        }
    
    async def handle_auto_commit_notification(self, 
                                   agent_id: str,
                                   branch_name: str,
                                   commit_message: str,
                                   files_changed: List[str],
                                   task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Handle notification that an agent has auto-committed code
        
        Args:
            agent_id: Agent that made the commit
            branch_name: Branch that was committed to
            commit_message: Commit message
            files_changed: List of files that were changed
            task_id: Optional task ID
            
        Returns:
            Processing result
        """
        # Register the commit in our branch tree
        result = await self._register_external_commit(
            branch_name=branch_name,
            agent_id=agent_id,
            commit_hash="auto-commit",  # We don't have the real hash
            commit_message=commit_message,
            files_changed=files_changed,
            task_id=task_id
        )
        
        # Save branch tree
        self._save_branch_tree()
        
        return result

    def _is_strategy_request(self, text: str) -> bool:
        """Check if a message is related to strategy decisions"""
        strategy_keywords = [
            "strategy", "gitflow", "trunk-based", "branching strategy",
            "workflow", "process", "methodology", "approval", "review",
            "merge approval", "authorization", "permissions", "roles",
            "branch tree", "branch structure", "branch hierarchy"
        ]
        
        text_lower = text.lower()
        
        # Check for strategy keywords
        for keyword in strategy_keywords:
            if keyword in text_lower:
                return True
                
        return False

            "branch": branch_name,
            "commit_hash": commit_hash,
            "agent_id": agent_id,
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "message": commit_message,
            "files_changed": files_changed,
            "task_id": task_id
        })
        
        # Check if we need to run tests
        if self.ci_cd_config["run_tests"] and self.ci_cd_config["enabled"]:
            # Running tests on auto-commit is optional depending on CI/CD settings
            if self.ci_cd_config.get("test_on_commit", True):
                # Run tests asynchronously (don't wait for results here)
                asyncio.create_task(self.run_tests_on_branch(branch_name, task_id or "unknown"))
        
        return {
            "status": "success",
            "message": f"Registered commit {commit_hash[:7]} on branch {branch_name}",
            "branch_name": branch_name,
            "agent_id": agent_id,
            "run_tests": self.ci_cd_config["run_tests"] and self.ci_cd_config.get("test_on_commit", True)
        }
        
    async def setup_agent_auto_commit_hook(self, agent_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Set up auto-commit hook for an agent
        
        Args:
            agent_id: Agent ID to set up hook for
            
        Returns:
            Setup result
        """
        # This would typically be implemented by injecting a post-edit hook
        # into the agent's workflow that calls back to this agent
        
        # For now, we'll just return success and assume each agent will notify us
        return {
            "status": "success",
            "message": f"Auto-commit hook set up for agent {agent_id}",
            "agent_id": agent_id
        }
    
    async def handle_auto_commit_notification(self, 
                                   agent_id: str,
                                   branch_name: str,
                                   commit_message: str,
                                   files_changed: List[str],
                                   task_id: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Handle notification that an agent has auto-committed code
        
        Args:
            agent_id: Agent that made the commit
            branch_name: Branch that was committed to
            commit_message: Commit message
            files_changed: List of files that were changed
            task_id: Optional task ID
            
        Returns:
            Processing result
        """
        # Register the commit in our branch tree
        result = await self._register_external_commit(
            branch_name=branch_name,
            agent_id=agent_id,
            commit_hash="auto-commit",  # We don't have the real hash
            commit_message=commit_message,
            files_changed=files_changed,
            task_id=task_id
        )
        
        # Save branch tree
        self._save_branch_tree()
        
        return result

import json
from typing import Dict, List, Any, Optional
import re

from hive_mind.agent_sdk.base_agent import BaseAgent, Message

class EfficiencyCriticAgent(BaseAgent):
    """
    Efficiency Critic Agent that analyzes implementations for performance issues, 
    inefficiencies, and resource wastage.
    This agent has a skeptical personality that constantly looks for optimization opportunities.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, 
                agent_id: str = "efficiency_critic", 
                model: str = "gpt-4o", 
                temperature: float = 0.4,  # Lower temperature for more analytical output
                token_limit: int = 4096):
        """
        Initialize the Efficiency Critic Agent
        
        Args:
            agent_id: Unique identifier for the agent
            model: LLM model to use
            temperature: LLM temperature setting (lower for more analytical output)
            token_limit: Maximum token limit for LLM calls
        """
        super().__init__(agent_id, model, temperature, token_limit)
        self.identified_inefficiencies: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}
        self.optimization_suggestions: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
        self.efficiency_scores: Dict[str, float] = {}
        
    async def process_message(self, message: Message) -> Message:
        """
        Process an incoming message and generate a response
        
        Args:
            message: The incoming message
            
        Returns:
            A response message with efficiency concerns
        """
        if message.message_type == "task_assignment":
            return await self._handle_task_assignment(message)
        elif message.message_type == "efficiency_review":
            return await self._handle_efficiency_review(message)
        elif message.message_type == "question":
            return await self._handle_question(message)
        else:
            # Default handling for other message types
            prompt = await self.generate_prompt({
                "message": message.content,
                "sender": message.sender,
                "context_tags": message.context_tags,
                "type": "default"
            })
            
            response = await self.call_llm(prompt)
            
            return await self.send_message(
                recipients=[message.sender],
                content=response["content"],
                context_tags=message.context_tags + ["#efficiency", "#performance", "#skeptical"],
                message_type="response",
                thread_id=message.thread_id
            )
    
    async def _handle_task_assignment(self, message: Message) -> Message:
        """
        Handle a task assignment message
        
        Args:
            message: The task assignment message
            
        Returns:
            A response message
        """
        task_prompt = await self.generate_prompt({
            "task": message.content,
            "thread_id": message.thread_id,
            "context_tags": message.context_tags,
            "type": "task_assignment"
        })
        
        response = await self.call_llm(task_prompt)
        content = response["content"]
        
        # Create status update for the manager
        return await self.send_message(
            recipients=[message.sender],
            content=f"I will analyze this task for efficiency implications. Initial concerns: {self._extract_initial_concerns(content)}",
            context_tags=["#efficiency", "#performance", "#skeptical", "#status_update"],
            message_type="status_update",
            thread_id=message.thread_id
        )
    
    async def _handle_efficiency_review(self, message: Message) -> Message:
        """
        Handle an efficiency review request
        
        Args:
            message: The review message containing code or design to analyze
            
        Returns:
            A response message with efficiency findings
        """
        review_prompt = await self.generate_prompt({
            "content_to_review": message.content,
            "sender": message.sender,
            "context_tags": message.context_tags,
            "type": "efficiency_review"
        })
        
        response = await self.call_llm(review_prompt)
        content = response["content"]
        
        # Extract inefficiencies and store them
        inefficiencies = self._extract_inefficiencies(content, message.thread_id)
        
        # Calculate an efficiency score based on findings
        impact_values = {
            "critical": 10.0,  # Critical performance issue
            "high": 7.0,       # Major inefficiency
            "medium": 4.0,     # Noticeable inefficiency
            "low": 1.0,        # Minor inefficiency
            "micro": 0.5       # Micro-optimization opportunity
        }
        
        total_impact = sum(impact_values.get(i.get("impact", "medium"), 4.0) for i in inefficiencies)
        # Score is inversely proportional to total impact (higher impact = lower score)
        efficiency_score = max(0, 10.0 - min(total_impact, 10.0))
        self.efficiency_scores[message.thread_id] = efficiency_score
        
        # Store any optimization suggestions
        self.optimization_suggestions[message.thread_id] = self._extract_optimizations(content)
        
        return await self.send_message(
            recipients=[message.sender],
            content=content,
            context_tags=message.context_tags + ["#efficiency", "#performance", "#optimization", "#skeptical"],
            message_type="efficiency_findings",
            thread_id=message.thread_id
        )
    
    async def _handle_question(self, message: Message) -> Message:
        """
        Handle a question message
        
        Args:
            message: The question message
            
        Returns:
            A response message with an efficiency-focused answer
        """
        question_prompt = await self.generate_prompt({
            "question": message.content,
            "sender": message.sender,
            "context_tags": message.context_tags,
            "type": "question"
        })
        
        response = await self.call_llm(question_prompt)
        
        return await self.send_message(
            recipients=[message.sender],
            content=response["content"],
            context_tags=message.context_tags + ["#efficiency", "#performance", "#skeptical"],
            message_type="answer",
            thread_id=message.thread_id
        )
    
    async def generate_prompt(self, context: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        """
        Generate a prompt for the LLM based on the provided context
        
        Args:
            context: Context for prompt generation

            Generated prompt
        """
        if context.get("type") == "task_assignment":
            return f"""
            You are the Efficiency Critic of an AI development team. You have a personality that's laser-focused on performance, optimization, and resource efficiency. You question every implementation decision from an efficiency standpoint.
            
            Task to Analyze: {context.get('task', '')}
            Context Tags: {', '.join(context.get('context_tags', []))}

            2. Likely resource inefficiencies (CPU, memory, I/O, network)

            """
        elif context.get("type") == "efficiency_review":

            4. Always considers scalability and resource consumption
            5. Analytical and data-driven in your criticism
            
            Perform a thorough efficiency review, addressing:
            1. Identified inefficiencies (with impact: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Micro)
            2. Algorithm complexity and scaling behavior (Big O analysis where applicable)
            3. Resource consumption concerns (memory, CPU, I/O, network)
            4. Potential bottlenecks under load
            5. Specific optimization recommendations
            6. Benchmarking suggestions to verify performance
            
            Format your findings with clear headings and bullet points. Be analytical, thorough, and focused on measurable improvements.
            """
        elif context.get("type") == "question":
            return f"""
            You are the Efficiency Critic of an AI development team. You have a personality that's laser-focused on performance, optimization, and resource efficiency.

            Context Tags: {', '.join(context.get('context_tags', []))}
            
            Your personality traits:
            1. Obsessed with performance optimization and resource efficiency
            2. Assumes there are inefficiencies in every implementation
            3. Questions design choices that could lead to performance bottlenecks
            4. Always considers scalability and resource consumption
            5. Analytical and data-driven in your criticism
            
            Provide an efficiency-focused answer that:
            1. Questions assumptions about performance in the question
            2. Highlights potential efficiency concerns
            3. Suggests more optimized approaches
            4. References algorithmic complexity and resource usage
            
            Be analytical yet helpful, precise yet clear.
            """
        else:
            # Default prompt
            return f"""
            You are the Efficiency Critic of an AI development team. You have a personality that's laser-focused on performance, optimization, and resource efficiency.

            Your personality traits:
            1. Obsessed with performance optimization and resource efficiency
            2. Assumes there are inefficiencies in every implementation
            3. Questions design choices that could lead to performance bottlenecks
            4. Always considers scalability and resource consumption
            5. Analytical and data-driven in your criticism
            
            Respond with an efficiency-focused perspective that challenges assumptions and highlights optimization opportunities.
            """
    
    def _extract_inefficiencies(self, content: str, thread_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Extract inefficiencies from the LLM response
        
        Args:
            content: LLM response content
            thread_id: Current thread ID
            
        Returns:
            List of inefficiencies with metadata
        """
        inefficiencies = []
        
        # Look for inefficiency sections
        inefficiency_pattern = r"(?:Inefficiency|Performance Issue|Bottleneck|Optimization)(?:[:\s]+)([^\n]+)"
        inefficiency_matches = re.finditer(inefficiency_pattern, content, re.IGNORECASE)
        
        for match in inefficiency_matches:
            issue_title = match.group(1).strip()
            
            # Look for impact indicators
            impact = "medium"  # Default
            impact_patterns = {
                r"\b(?:critical|severe|extreme)\b": "critical",
                r"\bhigh\b": "high",
                r"\bmedium\b": "medium",
                r"\blow\b": "low",
                r"\bmicro(?:-optimization)?\b": "micro"
            }
            
            for pattern, level in impact_patterns.items():
                if re.search(pattern, issue_title, re.IGNORECASE):
                    impact = level
                    break
            
            # Determine resource type
            resource_type = "general"
            resource_types = {
                r"\b(?:cpu|processor|compute)\b": "cpu",
                r"\b(?:memory|ram|heap|stack)\b": "memory",
                r"\b(?:io|disk|storage|file)\b": "io",
                r"\b(?:network|bandwidth|latency|throughput)\b": "network",
                r"\b(?:database|query|sql)\b": "database",
                r"\b(?:algorithm|complexity|big[ -]?o)\b": "algorithm"
            }
            
            for pattern, res_type in resource_types.items():
                if re.search(pattern, issue_title, re.IGNORECASE):
                    resource_type = res_type
                    break
            
            inefficiencies.append({
                "title": issue_title,
                "impact": impact,
                "resource_type": resource_type,
                "thread_id": thread_id,
                "timestamp": __import__('time').time()
            })
        
        # Store inefficiencies
        self.identified_inefficiencies[thread_id] = inefficiencies
        return inefficiencies
    
    def _extract_optimizations(self, content: str) -> List[str]:
        """
        Extract optimization suggestions from the LLM response
        
        Args:
            content: LLM response content
            
        Returns:
            List of optimization suggestions
        """
        optimizations = []
        
        # Look for optimization sections
        opt_pattern = r"(?:Optimization|Improvement|Recommendation)(?:[:\s]+)([^\n]+)"
        opt_matches = re.finditer(opt_pattern, content, re.IGNORECASE)
        
        for match in opt_matches:
            opt = match.group(1).strip()
            if opt and len(opt) > 10:  # Avoid short/empty optimizations
                optimizations.append(opt)
        
        # Also look for bulleted optimizations
        bullet_opt_pattern = r"[\*\-•] ([^:]+: [^\n]+)"
        bullet_matches = re.finditer(bullet_opt_pattern, content)
        
        for match in bullet_matches:
            opt = match.group(1).strip()
            if "optimiz" in opt.lower() or "improv" in opt.lower() or "reduc" in opt.lower() or "better" in opt.lower():
                if opt and len(opt) > 10:
                    optimizations.append(opt)
        
        return optimizations
    
    def _extract_initial_concerns(self, content: str, max_items: int = 3) -> str:
        """
        Extract initial efficiency concerns from the LLM response
        
        Args:
            content: LLM response content
            max_items: Maximum number of concerns to extract
            
        Returns:
            String with formatted initial concerns
        """
        concerns = []
        
        # Look for bulleted items which are likely concerns
        bullet_pattern = r"[\*\-•]([^\n]+)"
        bullet_matches = re.finditer(bullet_pattern, content)
        
        for match in bullet_matches:
            concern = match.group(1).strip()
            if concern and len(concern) > 10:
                concerns.append(concern)
                if len(concerns) >= max_items:
                    break
        
        # If we didn't find enough bulleted items, try to extract sentences
        if len(concerns) < max_items:
            sentence_pattern = r"([^.\n]+\.[^\n]*)"
            sentence_matches = re.finditer(sentence_pattern, content)
            
            for match in sentence_matches:
                sentence = match.group(1).strip()
                if sentence and len(sentence) > 10 and sentence not in concerns:
                    concerns.append(sentence)
                    if len(concerns) >= max_items:
                        break
        
        # Format the concerns
        if concerns:
            return "; ".join(concerns)
        else:
            return "Analyzing potential performance implications..."
            
    def calculate_complexity(self, algorithm_description: str) -> str:
        """
        Estimate the algorithmic complexity from a description
        
        Args:
            algorithm_description: Description of the algorithm
            
        Returns:
            Big O notation estimate
        """
        # This is a simple heuristic approach - in a real implementation,
        # this would be much more sophisticated
        
        complexity = "O(n)"  # Default to linear time
        
        # Look for common complexity indicators
        if re.search(r"\bloop\s+within\s+loop\b|\bnested\s+loop\b|\bfor\s+each.*?\bfor\s+each\b", algorithm_description, re.IGNORECASE):
            complexity = "O(n²)"
        elif re.search(r"\bsort\b|\bmerge\b|\bquicksort\b", algorithm_description, re.IGNORECASE):
            complexity = "O(n log n)"
        elif re.search(r"\bhash\b|\bdictionary\b|\blookup\b|\bconstant\b", algorithm_description, re.IGNORECASE):
            complexity = "O(1)"
        elif re.search(r"\blogarthmic\b|\bbinary\s+search\b|\bdivide\s+and\s+conquer\b", algorithm_description, re.IGNORECASE):
            complexity = "O(log n)"
        elif re.search(r"\bexponential\b|\brecursive\b|\bpermutation\b|\bcombination\b", algorithm_description, re.IGNORECASE):
            complexity = "O(2ⁿ)"
        
        return complexity
